Pennsylvania candidate for US Senate in 2028, Ahmed Moor, speaks in a video posted on his X account, on 12 November 2026 (Screengrab/@AhmedMoor)
Off
A 42-year-old Palestinian-American writer has emerged as the first challenger to Pennsylvania Democratic senator and staunch pro-Israel ally John Fetterman in his 2028 Senate race.
It's not too uncommon for US candidates to declare their bid this early. Election campaigns in this country run for at least 18 months before every election, giving voters little reprieve from the ads and media placements.
Speaking to Middle East Eye on Monday, Ahmed Moor said he is centring three foreign policy priorities. "End the war in Iran. End the war in Ukraine. End the war on the Palestinians."
The slogan echoes the successful platforms of those who undoubtedly paved the way for him: Democratic Socialist New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, and Democratic Michigan Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed.
Though in his conversation with MEE, he did not seem to want the comparison to be made.
Moor is also an immigrant, an Arab, a Muslim, a millennial, a progressive, a passionate proponent of Palestinian rights, and a father of three girls. Sayed has two children, and played up his "girl dad" persona.
Was Moor inspired?
"I'm a man of the left," he responded, sticking strictly to his campaign message. "We're going to have the left-right contest in America all the time. What this campaign is about is the shape of the sandbox. The idea that the Constitution and Bill of Rights is under assault is not a left-right issue. That's an American issue."

data.title: Middle East Eye: Israeli parliament elects Eisenkot ally as speaker in blow for Netanyahu
data.author: Bilge Kotan
data.summary:
Israeli parliament elects Eisenkot ally as speaker in blow for Netanyahu
Israeli lawmakers on Tuesday elected Matan Kahana, a parliament speaker from the camp opposed to caretaker prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
Sixty-six of 120 lawmakers voted in favour of Kahana, an ally of former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, who has until next month to form a government to replace Netanyahu.
Netanyahu's Likud party had put forward Ofir Katz as its own candidate, who received 52 votes.
The parliament speaker is an important office given that it sets the timetable for parliamentary business and can therefore speed up or delay debates or votes on proposed legislation.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Rubio says 'no imminent threat' to US from Iran
data.author: Mera Aladam
data.summary:
Rubio says 'no imminent threat' to US from Iran
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio cast doubt about reports of an "imminent threat" from Iran on Washington.
Speaking to reporters in the Philippines, Rubio said that US authorities routinely check for potential threats against the country, but added that most intelligence leads are not considered credible.
When asked if he was concerned about a possible attack on Washington, he said: "I am not. But again, we're concerned every day about anything that threatens our country ... I don't think there's any imminent threat.
"The United States is always on the lookout for anyone who tries to do harm to our country and to our people. And we have threat streams every day, and the majority of them are not credible. We have to follow up on them," Rubio added.
Rubio also questioned the credibility of sources cited in a CNN report about an alleged Iranian plot targeting the US capital, saying: "Some of your intelligence sources are liars; others are liars and criminals."
"I won't even comment on it because I don't know who's leaking this stuff to you guys. But they're either showboats and liars, or probably criminals if they're saying anything that's even half true."

data.title: Middle East Eye: Watch: Israeli settles kill Palestinian grandmother in occupied West Bank
data.author: Mera Aladam
data.summary:
Watch: Israeli settles kill Palestinian grandmother in occupied West Bank
Israeli settlers shot dead an elderly Palestinian woman and wounded eight of her family members during an attack outside her home in the village of Ein al-Duyuk al-Tahta, west of Jericho in the occupied West Bank.
According to eyewitnesses, armed settlers shot 73-year-old Fidda Fheidat in the head, killing her on the spot.
The settlers, who had recently seized eight Palestinian homes in an area adjacent to the village, went on to fire at other members of the family, wounding eight of them.
According to Jihad Mahalis, a member of the village’s local committee, the settlers have launched attacks on the village homes every single night since seizing the properties, which are located some 500 metres away from the rest of the village’s homes.

Thirty years after Rabin's assassination, Israel is again flirting with political violence
Submitted by
Lubna Masarwa
on
Tue, 11/17/2026 - 21:02
In the wake of elections that handed Arabs the balance of power, we are witnessing an unprecedented outpouring of hate speech and racism
Benjamin Netanyahu, then the Israeli opposition leader, addresses the Knesset in September 1993, two years before the assassination of Yitzhak Rabin (Menahem Kahana/AFP)
Off
A week before the recent Israeli elections, I took my 10-year-old nephew to a cinema in West Jerusalem. As we got into a lift in the car park, a young Israeli Jew entered holding an M16 rifle. Other Israeli Jews got in too.
When we got out on the cinema level, my nephew said with a smile: “I’ll give you 100 shekels if you dare to speak Arabic in the lift.”
Speaking Arabic in public has become a real issue in Israel. It’s the subject of panel debates on television, where speakers compete to express increasingly extreme views and to incite against Palestinian doctors, bus drivers and students.
A woman in the mixed Arab city of Yaffa told me she was afraid to use public transport in her town, fearing she would be attacked by Israeli groups.
This past summer, three Arab female employees were dismissed from a fashion store in Afula after refusing to comply with a branch manager’s ban on speaking Arabic at work.
Hate speech and racism dominate Israeli public life to a degree I have never witnessed before. Attacks by Israeli Jewish groups on Palestinians who speak Arabic, or on women who wear headscarves in the street, have become routine.
But the hatred is not directed solely at Palestinians. Secular Israelis attack Haredim, or ultra-Orthodox Jews, for not serving in the army; the Haredim attack coffee shops that open on Shabbat.

Trump lands in China for meeting with Xi and Putin
US President Donald Trump has arrived in China for the Apec summit in Shenzhen, where he is expected to meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladmir Putin.
The historic trilateral meeting between the leaders will take place on Thursday. Xi, Trump and Putin are due to meet on the sidelines of the summit to potentially discuss Russia's war with Ukraine and the US-Israeli war on Iran, as well as trade, AI and nuclear weapons.
Xi met Trump off the plane on the tarmac at Shenzhen, reciprocating Trump's gesture when the Chinese leader visited the US in September.
Xi told Trump he hoped their talks would help advance a “constructive, strategic and stable relationship” between China and the US, based on “respect, fairness and reciprocity”, according to China’s state news agency Xinhua.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said that Putin and Trump are unlikely to have time for fully fledged bilateral negotiations in China, but may talk on the event's sidelines, the Tass news agency reported.
Peskov was cited as saying that the two leaders would exchange views on the conflicts in Ukraine and Iran if they got a chance to talk one-on-one.
US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping (Reuters)

data.title: Middle East Eye: Iran launches attacks on military base in Kuwait
data.author: MEE staff
data.summary:
Iran launches attacks on military base in Kuwait
Submitted by
MEE staff
on
Wed, 11/18/2026 - 09:34
The Iranian army said it had targeted the Ali al-Salem Airbase in Kuwait, while the cause of a building fire in Bahrain is being investigated
Missiles are put on display in central Tehran on 28 September (AFP)
Off
Iran has launched a series of attacks against its Gulf neighbours in Kuwait and Bahrain, as tensions continue to simmer.
In a statement published on state media early on Wednesday, the Iranian army said it fired a drone targeting the Ali al-Salem Airbase in Kuwait.
"This morning, the Islamic Republic of Iran's army's destructive combat drones targeted Patriot defense systems and drone and missile launchers of the US terrorist army at the Ali al-Salem base in Kuwait with destructive drones," the statement read.
"In defense of Iran, we will not bow to any power, but our response to any threat or aggression will be decisive, crushing, and without geographical limitations," the army added
Earlier, the Kuwaiti ⁠⁠military said ⁠⁠that its air defences were ⁠⁠countering the ⁠⁠attack.
Kuwait’s Foreign Ministry described the attack as "repeated and criminal" adding that it was a "direct threat" to the Gulf country's "security and stability".
"The Ministry reaffirms that the continuation of these attacks constitutes a dangerous escalation that threatens the region’s security and stability and undermines diplomatic efforts aimed at de-escalation and reducing tensions," it said on X.
According to the ministry, Kuwait retains the right to "take all necessary measures to safeguard its sovereignty, preserve its security and defend its territory and vital facilities against any aggression or threat, in exercise of its inherent right to self-defence".
